description:
Construction of Castello di Gabbiano's defensive tower began in the year 1100 to protect one of the most important trade routes between Florence and Siena. The property's history as we know it today begins in 1124, when the Bardi family, influential Florentine bankers, built the first cellars within the castle's walls. By the late 13th century, the family had expanded the fortress, building walls on either side of the original tower in Guelph architectural style.

In the 15th century, Gabbiano passed from the Bardi family to the Soderini family. During the Soderini era, the "casa padronale" was converted into a farm of a structure similar to what survives today, as documented in a text written by Tommaso Soderini in 1464. Today the castle's imposing square tower crowns one of Chianti Classico's most important wine estates, with more than 370 acres of vineyards certified 100% sustainable.

The Bardi family's involvement — among the most powerful banking families of medieval Florence — connects Gabbiano's early winemaking history to the same financial networks that shaped Florentine commerce and politics well beyond this single estate.

The late 13th-century Guelph-style expansion of the fortress ties Gabbiano to the broader Guelph-Ghibelline political divide that shaped so much of medieval Tuscan architecture and territorial control.

The 1464 Soderini-era document describing the property's conversion to a farm structure gives Gabbiano an unusually precise documentary record of its architectural transition from fortress to agricultural estate, dated to a specific year rather than a general century.

The estate's 370+ acres of certified sustainable vineyards place Gabbiano among the more environmentally significant wine producers in Chianti Classico, alongside its historical pedigree.

faqs.question: Can I taste wine at Castello di Gabbiano without staying overnight?
faqs.answer: Yes — daily wine tastings and guided cellar tours are open to the public, with or without a room booking.

faqs.question: Are all the rooms at Castello di Gabbiano within the historic building?
faqs.answer: No — 11 Tuscan Renaissance-style rooms and suites are in the historic building, while independent apartments with full amenities are elsewhere on the estate.

faqs.question: Who were the Bardi family?
faqs.answer: Influential Florentine bankers who built the castle's first cellars in 1124, laying the foundation for its winemaking history.

hotel.how_to_stay:
**Getting there:** About 10 minutes from Mercatale Val di Pesa and 30 minutes from Florence by car; Florence's Peretola Airport (FLR) is about 35 minutes away.

**Rooms & rates:** 11 Tuscan Renaissance-style rooms and suites in the historic building, plus independent apartments with full amenities elsewhere on the estate. From €254/night.

**On-site:** Own winery with daily tastings, guided tours of the historic cellar and educational vineyards, olive groves.

**Good to know:** One of Chianti Classico's most recognized wineries — ideal for combining a stay with serious wine tourism, not just a one-off tasting.

**Combine with:** Mercatale Val di Pesa (~10 min), San Casciano in Val di Pesa, Florence (~30 min), the Chianti Classico wine route.
